name: go-modules
title: go generate + modules
summary: Go's own answer, with no third-party build tooling: a `//go:generate` directive beside the code that consumes the output, and a `replace` directive pointing the module path at the generated tree. dsdlc writes `generated/go.mod`, so the output is a module and needs no packaging.
notes:
The `require` line names a version that is never fetched -- `replace` resolves the module from disk instead -- which is how you depend on an unpublished module without a registry, a vendor directory, or a network.

`go generate` does not type-check, so the directive runs happily on a clean checkout where `generated/` does not exist and the import cannot yet resolve. That is what makes generate-then-build work as a single ordered pass rather than needing a bootstrap.

requires.reason: runs go generate, compiles, and links
